item.title: ChatGPT dominates early AI spending in Congress as lawmakers weigh regulation
item.description:
- OpenAI’s ChatGPT accounted for about 88% of identifiable House spending on artificial intelligence tools during the year ending March 31, according to a CNBC analysis.
[OpenAI](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/09/open-ai-sam-altman-chatgpt-5-6-sol.html) is dominating the first visible wave of artificial intelligence spending inside [Congress](https://www.cnbc.com/congress/).
Other offices are also using AI to summarize [reports and bills](https://www.cnbc.com/legislation/), draft social media posts, prepare constituent responses, analyze legislation, review hearing materials and sort through policy research, according to Marci Harris, CEO of [POPVOX Foundation](https://popvox.com/), a nonprofit that helps train members of Congress and staff on how to use AI.

item.title: Master’s degree in artificial intelligence gets underway
item.description:
A new master’s degree in artificial intelligence (AI) being offered this fall at WSU will provide students with high-demand skills in AI and machine learning to meet industry needs around the state and region.
“Artificial intelligence and machine learning tools play a critical role in application development in many real-world engineering, science, and industrial domains, such as health or environmental informatics, physics, chemistry, additive manufacturing, bioinformatics, and cybersecurity,” said Doppa.
WSU’s School of EECS has a critical mass of faculty who are conducting cutting-edge research in AI and applied areas, ranging from AI for science and engineering, trustworthy AI, generative AI, and reinforcement learning, to interdisciplinary applications, such as the agriculture-focused [AI Institute for Transforming Workforce and Decision Support institute.](https://agaid.org/) The school has a strong [cybersecurity program](https://school.eecs.wsu.edu/academics/undergraduate-program/cybersecurity/) and is ranked among the [top computer science programs](https://csrankings.org/#/index?all&us) in the US in design automation, high-performance computing, and artificial intelligence.

item.title: BUILDING BRIDGES: Wisdom in the age of artificial intelligence [DR. JOSEPH E. WOODS COLUMN]
item.description:

(Sebastien Bozon/AFP/Getty Images North America/TNS) ](https://www.trentonian.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/202607290400MCT_____PHOTO____OPED-GENAI-PLAY-COMMENTARY-FILEPIC-GET.jpg)
This illustration photograph taken in Mulhouse, eastern France on Feb. 11, 2025, shows the logo of OpenAI’s artificial intelligence chatbot ChatGPT.
Whether we find that fascinating, concerning, or difficult to understand, it is a reality in the age of advanced technology and artificial intelligence.
Social media delivers opinions every second, and artificial intelligence can produce essays, images, videos, campaign advertisements, and conversations that sound remarkably convincing with the push of a button.
Before we go any further, let’s define what we mean by artificial intelligence. IBM defines artificial intelligence (AI) as technology that enables computers and machines to simulate human learning, reasoning, problem-solving, and decision-making. Simply put, AI is a computer system designed to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.
Artificial intelligence can process information. AI can generate answers.
Artificial intelligence is no different.
AI is already helping doctors detect disease, advancing research, improving accessibility, and increasing productivity.
Artificial intelligence can process information.
Artificial intelligence is advancing at remarkable speed.
According to industry forecasts from organizations like McKinsey & Company and PwC, trillions of dollars are expected to be invested in artificial intelligence over the next few years. AI will continue to become more capable, but wisdom remains uniquely human because it requires character, discernment, and moral judgment.
